newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND CAN CUT INFLATION TO 13 PCT IN 97, IMF SAYS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND CAN CUT INFLATION TO 13 PCT IN 97, IMF SAYS.

text.p: The Polish government's plan to cut year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December 1997 from 18.5 percent last year while keeping 5.5 percent economic growth is realistic, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said.

But the IMF representative in Warsaw, Markus Rodlauer, said Poland should curb the recent growth of credit to bring domestic consuption under control. Otherwise the fight against inflation may be difficult, he suggested.
"I believe that gross domestic growth of 5-6 percent in 1997 is within reach, as is cutting inflation to 13 percent," Rodlauer told PAP news agency in an interview released on Sunday.
"I thing that the main task for today is reducing consumption, which would mean curbing credit," he added.
Poland saw a 40 percent growth of credit last year, with consumer loans doubling, which some analysts said showed that the country's economy was overheating.
The central bank has said it will implement a high interest rates policy this year to try to contain credit growth and help the government achieve its inflation goal.
